sections.summary: cairn status prints the stack and warnings; cairn approve records a human approval; Git.log reads task branches.
sections.title: `cairn status` and `cairn approve`

sections.summary: A commit-msg hook refuses a commit on a task branch without its Cairn-Task and Cairn-Section trailers, so every task commit can land.
sections.title: Trailer check

sections.summary: Builds `attemptsOf`, which derives each task's attempts (kind, outcome, cost and cost source) from its status events, plus per-task attempt and cost limits that make a task terminal, `taskCostOf` for summing a task's cost, and storage of raw usage reports in a new `usage_reports` table.
sections.title: Attempts

sections.summary: Defines the pure function `metricsOf`, which groups finished tasks by any combination of category, model, reasoning and harness and computes outcome metrics for each group, such as cost per verified task, first-pass rate, time to done, failure rates and cache use. Tasks with unknown cost are counted in `leftOut` and never treated as free.
sections.title: Outcome metrics

sections.summary: Builds the `cairn stats` command, which derives attempts from `events.jsonl` and prints per-category tables of outcome metrics for each model, reasoning level and harness. It also lists routed tasks and, in shadow mode, compares history recommendations with what ran. It has `--category`, `--since` and `--json` flags, and it is read-only and local.
sections.title: `cairn stats`

sections.summary: Builds the relation index: a pure `indexOf(source)` that pulls every kind of relation out of the manifest, spec index and PRD (or a trace), then answers queries over them. These cover neighbours, transitive needs, build order, whether a task can start, what it waits on, dangling ends and cycles.
sections.title: Relation index

sections.summary: Builds `sectionLinksOf`, a pure function that, for a PRD section or an ID'd list item, reports which other sections or items it needs and is needed by through task dependencies, and lists its unfinished tasks in build order, with a transitive mode as well.
sections.title: Section links

sections.summary: Makes the relation index the single source for what a task needs or waits on: lint gains a `need-cycle` error, the trace and `cairn status` report whether each task can start and what it waits on, stack layout reads from the index, and the viewer builds the same index from the trace.
sections.title: Answers from the index

sections.summary: Uses the restack conflict events the orchestrator already writes to events.jsonl as the conflict record, adds a pure calibrationOf function that counts conflicted restacks for high- and low-scoring pairs, and makes `cairn status` end with a one-line calibration summary.
sections.title: Conflict record

sections.summary: Groups the specification of session storage, redaction and the session command.
sections.title: Sessions

sections.summary: Specifies the SQLite trace store for redacted sessions, on Effect SQL's SqliteClient with Effect migrations; notes wait for their own migration.
sections.title: Trace store

sections.summary: Specifies redact(jsonl, secrets), which rewrites every decoded string value in a session log, its secret sources and fail-closed behaviour.
sections.title: Redaction

sections.summary: Specifies the `cairn session put` command, which redacts and stores a session log.
sections.title: `cairn session`

sections.summary: sessionOf(log, stored) in core reads a redacted Claude Code JSONL log into a Session, decoding only the fields it uses and taking file edits from toolUseResult.
sections.title: Reading a session

sections.summary: Reads Codex rollouts into per-call usage records (codexUsageOf), stores them idempotently in a new usage_calls table alongside session allocations and subagent links, and computes each task's usage total over distinct, share-weighted sessions (taskUsageOf), surfaced on TraceTask.usage.
sections.title: Usage records

sections.summary: Builds the pure function `estimateOf(calls, catalog)`. It prices each call in a session from the model catalog and returns an `Estimate`, labelled API-equivalent cost. The estimate is deterministic, works in integer micro-dollars, tracks which calls were priced, and records its rate sources, assumptions and excluded charges.
sections.title: API-equivalent cost

sections.summary: Builds subscription allowance and allocation estimates for subscription-billed sessions: Codex rate-limit snapshots are stored and turned into account use and per-session consumption (`allowanceOf`), and a configured subscription fee is optionally allocated across a period's sessions (`allocationOf`). Billed cost stays `null` throughout.
sections.title: Subscription allowance

sections.summary: Adds notes and review findings to Cairn: a `Note` contract type carried in the trace, a `notes` table, and the `cairn note add` and `cairn note resolve` commands that store notes anchored to link paths and attached to sessions.
sections.title: Notes

sections.summary: Lists what the existing orchestrator must do per task using only @cairn/contract/js and the CLI.
sections.title: Orchestrator adapter

sections.summary: Defines what the orchestrator adds to each task run: attempt metadata on the `running` event, a verify command run in the task's worktree that decides `done`, `blocked_on_human` or `failed` (with a failure kind), usage, cost and route on the final event, and session and usage recording through the cairn CLI. AGENTS.md documents these fields for adapter writers.
sections.title: Attempts and verification

sections.summary: Adds conflict-aware scheduling: a pure `scheduleOf` that orders ready tasks by conflict risk against running tasks, detects overlapping hunks between running tasks, and orders stack landing. It also covers the orchestrator behaviour (hold/release/notice/restack events, notices to agents, restacking on land) and how conflict events show in `cairn status` and the viewer timeline.
sections.title: Conflict-aware running

sections.summary: Specifies the single cairn binary built with effect/cli and the cairn init command.
sections.title: CLI

sections.summary: Builds the `cairn link` CLI command. It turns its arguments, in the order given, into viewer link steps and prints the encoded path, by default with the `cairn serve` origin. It checks sections, tasks, commits and roots before printing. The section also sets the rule that agents and the orchestrator name places with `cairn link`.
sections.title: `cairn link`

sections.summary: Builds the Cairn docs site, served under /docs/ on prdtrace.com beside the demo, for people setting Cairn up and for agents working in a repo. Its reference pages are generated from the code and it shows the real viewer.
sections.title: Documentation

sections.summary: Builds a build-time generator that writes the CLI reference pages from the `effect/cli` command definitions and the `.cairn/` file pages from the contract's generated JSON Schema. It also adds a check that fails the build when a docs page names a `cairn` command that no longer exists.
sections.title: Reference from code

sections.summary: Builds `apps/docs`, a Foldkit docs app. Its markdown pages render through the viewer's markdown renderer, it has sidebar navigation, and its search index is ranked by the viewer's matcher. Pages are prerendered to static HTML and deployed by `apps/site` under `/docs/`.
sections.title: Docs site

sections.summary: Builds the hand-written markdown pages of the documentation site: getting started, section IDs and done-when statements, planning, judging, human gates, cost per verified task, conflict-aware ordering, writing an orchestrator adapter, and the viewer with deep links.
sections.title: Pages

sections.summary: Lets a docs page embed the live demo viewer: a fenced `cairn-viewer` block holding a link path is rendered as a 640px-high iframe of the demo viewer at that path, showing this repo's own plan.
sections.title: The viewer on a page

sections.summary: Two git-backed routes on the dev server, GET /api/commits/:sha and GET /api/diffs/:base/:head, return a commit's patch and a task's whole diff as text for the code view.
sections.title: Patch routes

sections.summary: Specifies the cairn serve HTTP and WebSocket routes on port 4310 and how the viewer polls them.
sections.title: Server

sections.summary: Groups the viewer specification.
sections.title: Viewer

sections.summary: Specifies the viewer model, the messages every screen shares, the pure chainOf function, hovering a chain, and the three-pane layout.
sections.title: Model and messages

sections.summary: Specifies how the viewer renders markdown to Foldkit nodes without innerHTML.
sections.title: Markdown rendering

sections.summary: Specifies the viewer's design tokens for a light and a dark palette, its three stylesheets, the classes and controls every view is built from, and the move of the code view to them.
sections.title: Design system

sections.summary: Specifies the reader screen: the PRD read as a document in its own pane, with a status line under each heading, and the section at the top of the pane, or the pinned one, as the current section the other panes follow.
sections.title: Reader

sections.summary: Specifies the spec pane: one card per spec section that implements the current PRD section, with its summary, its tasks as rows inside it, and one control for how much of every card shows.
sections.title: Spec cards

sections.summary: Index and rank fuzzy matches for titles, IDs and branches.
sections.title: Fuzzy matching

sections.summary: Add search navigation and temporary chain highlighting.
sections.title: Search controls and chain highlighting

sections.summary: Search markdown prose with snippets and inline match highlights.
sections.title: Prose search and inline highlights

sections.summary: Specifies the curves that join the three panes for the current section: pure links and paths from measured rectangles, held inside their panes, measured by one Mount and lit along a chain on hover.
sections.title: Curves

sections.summary: Lays the stacks pane out like the spec's stack diagram: one numbered box per stack, a chip per task bottom to top inside it, and the boxes in rows over the base branch by what they wait on, with the current section's tasks standing out.
sections.title: Stacks

sections.summary: Specifies how the reader shows the model and reasoning each task ran with, or the plan's choice when it has not run, and the switch that shows or hides them everywhere.
sections.title: Models and reasoning

sections.summary: Specifies the dividers that resize the PRD pane, the spec pane and the detail panel by pointer or arrow keys, within limits, with the stacks pane taking what is left.
sections.title: Panes

sections.summary: Presence says which PRD section each participant is reading, shown as a chip beside that heading; pointer cursors stay on the canvas until it is removed, since no two reader windows could place one alike.
sections.title: Presence in the reader

sections.summary: Specifies the detail panel over the right of the reader: a trail of nodes, and for a task its status, what ran, its parent and dependencies, gate reasons, code, commits, traces and timeline.
sections.title: Detail panel

sections.summary: The code view screen: a stack tree, the selected task's whole diff or one commit's diff, and the session pane, opened from the detail panel and left with Back to the plan.
sections.title: Code view

sections.summary: Renders a task's whole diff or one commit's diff with @pierre/diffs: parsePatchFiles into FileDiffMetadata, one vanilla CodeView in a Foldkit Mount, syntax-highlighted through the Highlights backend.
sections.title: Diff view

sections.summary: The session pane draws the selected commit's session: notes and redaction counts, prompts and replies as markdown, and each tool call as one line that opens.
sections.title: Session pane

sections.summary: attributionOf(files, session) traces each hunk's changed lines to the last tool turn whose edit wrote them, and the diff and session pane link through those marks.
sections.title: Hunks and turns

sections.summary: Specifies the code and the agent session inside a task's detail: its whole stacked diff in the code view's mount, and the first prompt and tool calls of its latest commit's session.
sections.title: Code in the detail panel

sections.summary: Makes the reader the only plan screen and deletes the canvas with everything only it uses, after a human approves the loss of pan and zoom, dragging, coloured pins and pointer cursors.
sections.title: Replacing the canvas

sections.summary: Specifies the demo: a Trace generated from this repo's own .cairn/, what ran on its running events, and the commit patches its build ships as static files so the demo shows code without a server.
sections.title: Demo data

sections.summary: Every place the reader and the code view can open gets a deep link written with `LinkFromPath`. The section covers resolving a link against the trace and loaded data, opening it with the address bar and history kept in sync, and a "Copy link" action on every step. The canvas screen has no links.
sections.title: Deep links

sections.summary: Builds the pure `resolveLink` function in the viewer. It walks a deep link's steps against the trace and the loaded patches and sessions, and returns which steps resolved, which step is waiting for data, and what is missing. The section also builds `linkNoticeView`, the status notice that says how far a link opened and what is missing.
sections.title: Resolving a link

sections.summary: Makes the viewer a Foldkit application that owns the URL: it defines the viewer's only route, `linkRoute`, and `linkOf(model)`, which gives the canonical link of what is on screen. It also defines `openLink`, which applies a link step by step and fetches missing patches and sessions, and `withAddress`, which writes one browser history entry per step so Back walks the trail.
sections.title: Opening a link

sections.summary: Adds copy-link buttons across the viewer (PRD headings, spec cards, passages, the detail trail, stack boxes, the code view, diff lines and session turns). The buttons copy the same deep link the address bar holds, or a shorter link that opens one step on its own. The section also defines the pure `aloneOf` function in `links.ts`, which builds that shortest link.
sections.title: Copying a link

sections.summary: Makes list items that carry an ID behave in the viewer like small sections inside their section. Each such item gets a coverage annotation and a copyable ID. Items can be hovered, pinned and linked from spec cards and task rows, and their coverage counts toward the section's own counts.
sections.title: List items

sections.summary: Builds a pure cost module (compact estimate label, per-card cost sum over distinct sessions, per-allowance percentages) and shows usage and cost on the viewer's detail panel, task rows and card headers, including narrow widths and keyboard access.
sections.title: Cost on the graph

sections.summary: Adds an attempts list to the task detail panel, below the cost block, with one row per attempt, a line for a task that stopped at its attempt limit, and under the list the routing decision that chose the task's model, taken from the trace's `model` and `history` judgments.
sections.title: Attempts in the detail panel

sections.summary: Adds dependency links to the viewer: each heading and item shows how many sections it needs and how many need it, plus how many of its tasks are ready. A links button opens a list under the heading of what it needs, what needs it, and its next tasks. The task detail panel gains a `Needed by` list and says whether a pending task can start.
sections.title: What depends on what

sections.summary: Builds a ⌘K-style command menu for the viewer in Foldkit: a modal dialog opened by ⌘K/Ctrl+K, `/` or the toolbar search button. It lists commands, tasks, and PRD and spec matches ranked by the same fuzzy search index as the toolbar search. It also has nested search pages, keyboard navigation, chain preview and an accessible combobox/listbox view.
sections.title: Command menu

sections.summary: Builds read-only display of notes in the viewer: a pure `notesOf` function places each note by how far its anchor resolves (PRD passage, spec card, task row and chip, or diff line). Notes whose anchor does not fully resolve go into missing lists. The section also covers the note marker, count badges, diff annotations and a switch that shows resolved notes.
sections.title: Notes

sections.summary: Groups the model-based tests: the tools, then one model per piece of code tested against it.
sections.title: Testing

sections.summary: Adds @xstate/test on xstate 6.0.0-beta.5 and sets how a model test is written, seeded, covered and replayed.
sections.title: Model-based tests

sections.summary: Tests the presence server over real WebSockets against the room machine, so every participant sees the machine's room.
sections.title: Presence against the room machine

sections.summary: Tests the viewer's update against two machines written from the spec: the detail trail with pinning and Escape, and the pane dividers.
sections.title: Reader interactions against models

sections.summary: Tests derive against a machine of what an orchestrator writes and what git shows, which keeps facts and replays them as derive recomputes.
sections.title: Derivation against a model of its inputs

sections.summary: Maps each PRD acceptance criterion to how it is checked.
sections.title: Acceptance
